test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the classical feature of Ashokan pillars? Greitas zivitat amestu fatuan aur 8?

options.text: They had capitals topped with lion sculptures.
They were only found in South India.
They were made of bronze and silver.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They had capitals topped with lion sculptures.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ashokan pillars are a series of monolithic stone columns built during the reign of Emperor Ashoka, who ruled the Maurya Empire from 268–232 BCE.
 
• A defining feature of these pillars is their capitals, which are often topped with sculptures of animals, most famously lions, symbolizing strength, courage, and the spread of Dharma.
 
• The most renowned example is the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath, which features four lions seated back-to-back and serves as the national emblem of India today.
 
• The pillars were also inscribed with Ashoka's edicts, which communicated ethical and moral principles rooted in Buddhism.
 
• The Ashokan pillars were masterfully crafted using highly polished sandstone, showcasing exceptional Mauryan artistry and craftsmanship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: They were only found in South India.**
 
 
• This is incorrect as Ashokan pillars were primarily located in northern and central India, including regions like Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat.
 
• They were strategically placed near important trade routes, cities, and sites of Buddhist significance to ensure Ashoka's messages reached a wide audience.
 
• South India, while influenced by Ashokan policies, does not have any known Ashokan pillars.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: They were made of bronze and silver.**
 
 
• This is incorrect as Ashokan pillars were constructed from sandstone, not metals like bronze or silver.
 
• The sandstone used was often sourced from quarries in Chunar (Uttar Pradesh) or Mathura and transported to the pillar sites.
 
• The smooth polish and intricate carvings on these pillars highlight the technological advancements of the Mauryan era.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: They served as fire altars.**
 
 
• This is incorrect as the purpose of Ashokan pillars was not religious rituals involving fire but rather to disseminate the principles of Dhamma (moral law).
 
• The inscriptions on the pillars emphasized non-violence, respect for all living beings, and the promotion of social harmony.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Ashokan Pillars**
 
 
• The Ashokan pillars are among the earliest known examples of monumental stone art in India.
 
• They reflect Emperor Ashoka's adoption of Buddhism and his efforts to propagate its principles through visual and textual means.
 
• These pillars remain an enduring symbol of India's cultural and historical heritage.
